The measured inequalities in the cancer care pathway appear primarily at the **screening** stage. Evidence shows observed participation gaps in breast and cervical cancer screening by region, education level, and native language:

- Regional breast screening participation differences of up to 9.5 percentage points (e.g., 74.3% in Helsinki vs. 85.6% in North Ostrobothnia) are documented (S4).

- Cervical screening participation varies by education, with a 30.5 percentage-point difference between primary/unknown education (50.3%) and tertiary education (80.8%) groups (S4).

- Cervical screening participation also differs by native language, with a 19.7 percentage-point gap between domestic-language (76.5%) and other/missing language groups (56.8%) (S4).

Regarding later stages such as referral, diagnosis, and treatment, the evidence notes a **data gap**: comparable, nationwide, measured statistics on referral delays, diagnosis-to-treatment intervals, and treatment access are not yet available or published (S1, S3). Qualitative documentation exists about differences in access and treatment pathways, but no measured nationwide CSV data or verified statistics are currently supplied (S3).

In summary, the **screening stage** shows measured, observed inequalities, while the **referral, diagnostic follow-up, and treatment stages** currently lack comparable, validated nationwide data to quantify inequalities. Thus, measured inequalities appear at the screening stage, with data gaps preventing firm conclusions about later stages (S1, S3, S4).

# Evidence-Based Equity Gaps and Decision Support Candidates

## 1. Regional breast-screening participation gap — observed 2024

The Finnish Cancer Registry reports **81.6%** breast screening participation nationwide (excluding Åland), compared with **74.3% in the City of Helsinki**, **76.1% in West Uusimaa** and **85.6% in North Ostrobothnia**. The difference between these last two regional observations is **9.5 percentage points**.

**Source:** [Breast cancer screening programme: annual statistics 2024](https://stats.cancerregistry.fi/joukkistilastot/breast.html).

**What is demonstrated:** differences in screening-programme participation rates across regions.
